- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.23) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., sentiment < -0.16) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model exhibits strong lag in price declines — true drops often occur 2–3 days before forecasted.
- Forecast tends to overreact to recent price spikes — especially when sentiment is positive and price is rising.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high in the medium term (10–20 days) after a spike, ignoring sentiment-driven correction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often underestimates the downward trend — especially in the 10–15 day horizon.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence — model often fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility in the final 5–7 days.
